interfaces.name: Root air drying
interfaces.function: Assemble a reusable stone-and-bark tray, process actual roots and allow weather-dependent drying with reversible preservation while sufficiently dry.
interfaces.costs: Build: two stone units and one bark, two rounds at one energy. Load: up to two original root units, two crushing rounds per raw root at one energy. Already crushed compatible food needs one transfer round, with its prior costs and composition preserved. Unload/dismantle: one round and one energy. Passive weather exchange costs no actor rounds.
interfaces.effects: Food begins at its represented composition or the reviewed 50% root water assumption. Uncovered dry weather at 10–40 C removes at most 0.005 water mass per root per round to fraction 0.12; rain returns up to 0.01 per root, capped at original water. At fraction <=0.12 decay is 0.35 baseline, otherwise crushed food is 1.25 baseline. Exposure continues after unloading. No lost nutrients, reverse spoilage, sterilization or free materials.

execution.progress: Exact processId, actual site, escrow, reusable tools, paid energy and remaining work. Continue resumes; changing actions or lost reach pauses. Cancel/death releases actual material once without effort refunds.

personalIntent.progress: Health is 100, satiety 85.5, and two roots remain. The drying contract is available; no tray or preservation result exists yet.
personalIntent.next: Approach the remembered western tree and observe it, revealing nearby terrain along the route.

shown.question: Can harvested roots be preserved safely with locally obtainable materials?
evidence: At tick 25, root-air-drying is personally mastered.
The contract requires two stone units and one bark for a reusable tray.
Drying is weather-dependent; wet crushed roots decay at 1.25 baseline until sufficiently dry.
At tick 25, inventory contains two roots and no tray materials.
shown.uncertainty: Material sources and practical drying time under changing weather remain untested.
shown.goal: Build and test a tray using actual materials without endangering near-term nutrition.
completedSteps: Obtained and mastered the root-air-drying contract.
shown.missing: Two stone units, one bark, a suitable site and an actual drying trial.
shown.next: Explore west and inspect the remembered tree for useful observed properties.
shown.benefit: No preservation benefit has yet been demonstrated.

shown.question: Can I obtain a reserve of known safe food?
evidence: At tick 6, inventory contains four roots harvested at tick 2.
Starting knowledge gives roots 14 nutrition and zero toxicity.
shown.uncertainty: Storage longevity and source replenishment remain unknown.
shown.goal: Obtain four roots for near-term meals.
outputs: Four roots in personal inventory at tick 6.
shown.missing: Long-term storage and replenishment are untested.
shown.next: Consume as needed and monitor actual spoilage.
shown.benefit: Known safe food is available without immediate further gathering.

shown: Tick 25: two roots remain; roots provide 14 nutrition and have known zero toxicity.
The remembered western tree was observed at tick 3 with branch stock; bark availability is unknown.
Root drying needs substantial passive exposure and does not reverse spoilage.
